To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the information bottleneck theory is correct, and that DNNs compress the information flow during training.
(i) I(X;T), the mutual information between input X and internal representation T, does not compress in deterministic DNNs.

(1) the true I(X,T) over deterministic DNNs is vacuous; (2) the estimated mutual information in past works is a good measure of geometric clustering of hidden units; and (3) the compression phenomenon is driven by progressive geometric clustering of hidden unit representations of inputs from a single class.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the information-theoretic analysis of deep learning.
the evolution of internal DNN representations, and the information-theoretic quantities that are associated with it
the following three main questions. (1) How to properly estimate I(X;T), (2) What is the true quantity that is estimated in past works, (3) What is the underlying cause for the observed compression.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
The compression of the mutual information between the inputs X and internal representations of a DNN T, is not a phenomenon observed by any of the previous works.

the information flow in DNNs is indeed compressible, as the mutual information between input and internal representations decreases during training, but only because the hidden representations cluster.

the information bottleneck theory is indeed relevant to deep learning, and that the compression phenomenon observed in past works can be explained by a clustering of the hidden representations of inputs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

while the information bottleneck theory is not directly applicable to DNNs, its geometric interpretation can be used to study the compression of internal representations during training, and that the clustering phenomenon observed in past works is indeed the main driver of compression.
we show that compression of the estimated mutual information is a proxy for the geometric clustering of the hidden representations.

the information bottleneck theory provides a framework for analyzing the compression of internal representations, but the true quantity of interest is the mutual information between the hidden representations and the input class labels, and not between the hidden representations themselves.
Information Flow and Deep Networks
The main takeaway from our work is that
the information bottleneck theory can indeed explain the compression of DNNs, but the theory should be applied to a noisy DNN, which is shown here to be a good approximation of the original DNN.
the compression of I(X; T) observed in past works is not a property of DNNs per se, but rather a property of the specific estimator employed.
the information-theoretic quantities used in the information bottleneck theory are not directly applicable to deterministic DNNs.
